extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: An open-source multimodal interleaved dataset containing free-form sequences of images and text. It comprises one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images sourced from HTML, PDFs, and ArXiv papers.
extraction.creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from CommonCrawl dumps for HTML and PDF documents and from ArXiv source dumps for ArXiv documents, then parsed into multimodal documents and filtered with rules-based quality, safety, and deduplication procedures. HTML documents were extracted from CommonCrawl WARC files by parsing DOM trees; PDF links were extracted from CommonCrawl WAT files and downloaded/read; ArXiv documents were built from LaTeX source code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No missing information in individual instances was reported.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of HTML, PDF, and ArXiv multimodal documents from CommonCrawl and ArXiv. Released instances contain document text plus image URLs for HTML, and text plus the PDF URL and image reference numbers for PDFs and ArXiv documents.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024; included web data spans 2013 to 2024.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may still contain biases from public web data, and the creators explicitly avoid text quality classifier models because such models have been shown to favor text from certain demographics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is only provided as a training split, is not self-contained because it depends on external image URLs, and those URLs may disappear over time due to link rot. The full image-inclusive dataset is too large for the authors to host. The dataset may also contain confidential, offensive, personally identifying, and other sensitive public-web content despite filtering. It is not recommended for training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or sensitive content, nor for military applications.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to make research into large multimodal models more accessible, but the authors warn about risks of unfair treatment, stereotyping, privacy harms, and other harms, and advise additional filtering depending on the use case.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Potentially includes personally identifiable and sensitive information from the public web, including images of individuals, text about specific individuals, email addresses, IP addresses, and possibly sensitive attributes such as race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, locations, financial or health data, biometric or genetic data, government identification, and criminal history. Subpopulation information may also be extractable.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primarily intended for training large multimodal models; the dataset has only a training split. It can also be used for generating interleaved image-text sequences and building multimodal document retrieval systems. Users are encouraged to further filter the data based on their use case. Inappropriate uses include training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or sensitive content, and military applications.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is planned for public release, and the authors intend to release a repository linking papers or systems that use it. No explicit update schedule, maintainer details, or deprecation policy are provided.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Documents were made ML-ready through multimodal extraction and extensive filtering/cleaning: parsing HTML DOM trees from CommonCrawl, extracting and ordering PDF text/images, building ArXiv documents from LaTeX source, removing imports/bibliography/tables/citation tags, filtering non-English and low-quality text, removing NSFW/undesirable content, discarding invalid or extreme-size images, anonymizing emails and IP addresses, and deduplicating text and images.

inLanguage.evidence: Initially, we eliminate non-English documents using Fasttext’s [Joulin et al., 2017] language identification model

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The data comes from CommonCrawl dumps and is filtered using a series of rules-based heuristics and deduplication methods. The data is parsed from HTML and PDF documents that come from CommonCrawl and ArXiv dumps.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Data was obtained from a third party web crawl, CommonCrawl, for HTML and PDF documents and directly from ArXiv S3 buckets for ArXiv documents.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Is any information missing from individual instances? If so, please provide a description... None.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The released dataset contains HTML, PDF, and ArXiv multimodal documents... For HTML documents we release the document’s text along with image urls. For PDFs and ArXiv we also release the text along with the url for the PDF and a list of image reference numbers used to parse the images from the documents.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024. We include web data from 2013 to 2024.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We follow previous works in not using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. While we take steps to reduce biases and risks in our dataset

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: There is only a training split for MINT-1T. ... MINT-1T is not self-contained and relies on downloading external image urls to collect the full dataset. There are no guarantees these urls will remain available over time as link rot is a common problem for large scale image datasets. ... Using the dataset to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information ... as well as military applications are all inappropriate use cases of MINT-1T.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: MINT-1T was built to make research into large multimodal models more accessible. ... Is there anything that a dataset consumer might need to know to avoid uses that could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups (e.g., stereotyping, quality of service issues) or other risks or harms

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: We masked personally identifiable information such as emails and IP addresses to remove personal data from MINT-1T. ... it is possible to find images of individuals as well as text about specific individuals. ... Yes if it is present on the public web then it is possible such data is found in MINT-1T.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: There is only a training split for MINT-1T. ... Yes, we used MINT-1T to train large multimodal models ... The dataset can be used for other training objectives like generating interleaved images and text sequences or for building multimodal document retrieval systems. ... we encourage dataset consumers to further filter the data based on their use case. ... military applications are all inappropriate use cases

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We intend to release such a repository once we make the dataset public.
